suggestedTargetGuestSegments: The Inspired Professional: aged 28–55, urban, HHI $100–199k, allergic to boring traditional hotel experiences; balances intense career with exploration—novels, art, underground dining; expects seamless technology and flexible wellness/social/function in-room and public spaces.

fields.Brand Positioning: We exist to redefine the upper-upscale hospitality experience—challenging the norm with a stay that combines style with substance, innovation with comfort, and a sense of belonging in an elevated environment.
fields.Brand Customer Promise: Scandinavian-inspired design throughout offers comfort, distinctiveness, and warmth—dynamic, stimulating spaces that invite guests to spark imagination and transcend the ordinary.
fields.Brand Value Proposition:
Guests: Enticing Moments—subtle innovation that fosters belonging and discovery; familiar moments intertwined with the excitement of the new.

Owners: Iconic upper-upscale brand with global recognition and strong performance narrative in Americas flagship markets; pipeline and development support via Choice upscale platform.

Choice: Distinct upper-upscale brand for top urban and resort destinations—new build, adaptive reuse, and conversion.
fields.Key Brand Differentiators:
Enticing Moments (Experience): seamless environment fostering belonging and discovery—memorable stays through subtle innovation.

Nordic Nouveau (Design): Scandinavian-inspired comfort, distinctiveness, and warmth; style and purpose in dynamic, stimulating spaces.

Curatorial Warmth (Service): professional warmth akin to an art-gallery curator—confident, knowledgeable team inspiring discovery in an accessible environment.
fields.Brand Pillars:
Enticing Moments — experience pillar: belonging, discovery, memorable stays.

Nordic Nouveau — design pillar: Scandinavian-inspired, iconic inviting environments.

Curatorial Warmth — service pillar: curator-like warmth and confident hospitality.
fields.Guest Psychographics Description: Inspired Professionals find traditional spaces uninspired—forced to choose between design-forward-but-sterile or big-box-but-boring. They travel often, use public spaces for work and social transition, and expect guest rooms for decompression with seamless technology and surprise-and-delight features.
fields.Brand History: In 1960, Danish designer Arne Jacobsen's vision shaped the world's first design hotel—heritage that informs today's Radisson Blu upper-upscale positioning in urban and resort markets. Confirm historical claims in brand materials provided with your agreement.
